observed.traffic_context: lowest since May according to Kpler data cited by Reuters

semantic.interpretation: The shock has broadened from vessel attacks and impaired Hormuz traffic into potential refinery infrastructure risk. Commercial shipping remains directly exposed, while Iran's planned restricted Gulf zone and new Hormuz passage arrangements keep near-term route uncertainty elevated.

The energy shock is transmitting into bunker fuel and shipping costs rather than remaining only a crude-oil story. Asia is especially exposed because Singapore depends heavily on Gulf fuel-oil flows. Higher bunker costs can feed directly into container/bulk freight and indirectly into imported inflation for Taiwan.

observed.diplomacy_update: U.S. envoys reported possible new trilateral talks after Moscow and Kyiv visits; no breakthrough confirmed.

semantic.interpretation: Refinery damage is already visible in Russian fuel-oil exports, so the energy impact remains real. Renewed U.S.-mediated diplomacy is a modest de-escalation signal, but no settlement has been reached and winter energy infrastructure risk remains.

observed.taiwan_us_chip_policy_context: Taiwan manufacturers continue expanding U.S. investment while semiconductor tariff/export-control uncertainty remains material.

semantic.interpretation: This remains a structural rather than sudden shock: U.S. tariff and export-control policy can change Taiwan semiconductor capex geography, customer access, costs and supply-chain strategy.
